source_read: PMC HTML full text PMC4091648 (BMJ version of record), all sections; Tables 1 and 2 read as text; Figures 1-3 are images and their printed values were read on the PMC figure pages in my own tab; funding, independence and competing-interest statements read. The supplementary appendix (PDF) was not read: ischaemic stroke (fig S13), the >=1000-event analysis (table S10), definitions of binge drinking and abstention (table S2) and study designs are only there.

claims.overstatement: Minor. '56 European-descent studies' is the whole collaboration; the systolic estimate comes from 48 studies (227 559 people) and the number of studies behind the hypertension odds ratio is not printed. The reading that the non-drinker result 'points either to misreported drinking or to a path other than current drinking' is the editors' inference: the authors anticipated an attenuated effect in self-reported non-drinkers because long-term non-drinkers are hard to classify, but never discuss the non-drinker blood-pressure result itself. Reasonable, but it should be marked as the editors' reading.
claims.note: All Holmes numbers in statement and magnitude match the source: -0.88 mm Hg (-1.19 to -0.56); hypertension OR 0.94 (0.91 to 0.98) with 104 570 cases; 17.2% fewer units; strata -0.80 (none), -0.68 (>0 to <21 units/week), -1.70 (>=21). Comparison group (non-carriers, GG homozygotes) and units (UK units of 7.9 g; strata by self-reported current drinking) are right. The source gives no per-unit (instrumental-variable) estimate, so no per-gram figure comes from it. Not mentioned in the claim: by stratum, the hypertension odds ratio was clearly below 1 only in heavy drinkers (0.89, 0.81 to 0.99); in light-to-moderate drinkers it was 0.98 (0.93 to 1.03).

Methods › Statistical analysis, 5th paragraph; Discussion › Principal findings of study, 3rd paragraph
anchors.extracted: Authors expected no effect, or an attenuated one, in self-reported non-drinkers, noting that long-term non-drinkers are hard to classify by questionnaire. The Discussion states traits associated overall were null or much weaker in non-drinkers; the systolic panel of Figure 1 does not show this, and the paper does not discuss it.

claims.note: Only the phrase 'genetic studies do not find the lower risk' rests on this source, and Holmes supports it: carriers, who drank about 17% less, had no higher coronary odds in any drinking stratum. The test is weak at light intake: each stratum estimate is imprecise, a 17% proportional fall in a light drinker's intake is small, and no power calculation is given. The introduction's observational background (lowest risk at about 12-25 UK units a week against non-drinkers) is second-hand.

anchors.extracted: If the observational U-shape were causal, carriers were expected to have higher coronary risk at >0 to <21 units/week and lower at >=21. Observed OR 0.90 (0.79 to 1.02) at >0 to <7, 0.89 (0.75 to 1.06) at >=7 to <21, 0.97 (0.76 to 1.24) at >=21; trend P=0.828.

Second-hand background: cohort studies report lower cardiovascular risk with light to moderate drinking than with non-drinking, lowest at about 12-25 UK units a week; ill health among non-drinkers and confounding by lifestyle are named as alternative explanations.

claims.overstatement: Minor. '56 European-descent studies (261 991 people)' describes the collaboration; the coronary estimate rests on 46 studies with 168 731 people (Figure 2). 'The authors had predicted' is fair to the Methods, which state the expectation, but there is no published protocol showing it was written before the analysis.
claims.note: All Holmes numbers in statement and magnitude match: 17.2% (15.6% to 18.9%), binge OR 0.78 (0.73 to 0.84), abstention 1.27 (1.21 to 1.34), CHD 0.90 (0.84 to 0.96; 20 259 events; I2 17%), 0.81 (0.72 to 0.91) in four studies with >=1000 events (8374 events), non-drinkers 0.98 (0.88 to 1.10), drinkers 0.86 (0.78 to 0.94), P=0.095 (meta-regression), light 0.90 (0.79 to 1.02), moderate 0.89 (0.75 to 1.06), heavy 0.97 (0.76 to 1.24), trend P=0.83 (0.828 in the figure), systolic in non-drinkers -0.80 (-1.41 to -0.19), no instrumental-variable estimate. The comparison is A-allele carriers against GG homozygotes, and the units are UK units of 7.9 g. Instrument strength: very strong association with intake (P=5.5x10^-76) but no F statistic. Checks for other pathways: ever smoking OR 1.06 (1.02 to 1.09), education +0.04 SD, no link with physical activity or quantitative smoking, principal-component adjustment unchanged, and no linkage with known cardiovascular loci (Whitehall II only). One variant allows no pleiotropy-robust method. Coronary events include prevalent cases.

anchors.locator: Abstract (Participants); Methods › Formation of the consortium, 2nd paragraph; Results, 1st and 2nd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: 261 991 participants of European ancestry in 56 studies (56 of 59 approached); 48% women; mean age per study 58 (26 to 75); 20 259 coronary events, 10 164 strokes (4339 ischaemic).

Carriers v non-carriers: units/week -17.22% (-18.86 to -15.55; 46 studies, 218 969; I2 64%); top tertile OR 0.70 (0.68 to 0.73); binge drinking 0.78 (0.73 to 0.84; 21 studies); abstention 1.27 (1.21 to 1.34; 32 studies); gamma-glutamyltransferase -1.84% (-3.40 to -0.26).

anchors.locator: Figure 2; Results › Genetic association analysis › ADH1B and cardiovascular events, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: CHD OR 0.90 (0.84 to 0.96; 46 studies, 20 259 events in 168 731; I2 17%); four studies with >=1000 events 0.81 (0.72 to 0.91). Non-drinkers 0.98 (0.88 to 1.10; 5883 events), drinkers 0.86 (0.78 to 0.94; 10 130 events), P=0.095. Light 0.90 (0.79 to 1.02), moderate 0.89 (0.75 to 1.06), heavy 0.97 (0.76 to 1.24), P=0.828.

Stated expectation under a causal U-shape: higher coronary risk in light-to-moderate carriers, lower in heavy, no or weaker effect in non-drinkers. No instrumental-variable analysis, because available methods assume a linear relation.

anchors.extracted: Authors call the variant a non-specific proxy for volume, top-third drinking, binge drinking and abstention, so its associations reflect a mix of drinking patterns, not one.

claims.note: The claim reports Holmes correctly (all stroke 0.98, 0.90 to 1.07, 10 164 strokes; ischaemic 0.83, 0.72 to 0.95). This source does not support the headline that genetically higher intake goes with more stroke overall in people of European descent, because its all-stroke result was null. The ischaemic-stroke estimate comes from a subset (4339 cases) whose forest plot and study count are only in the appendix, and the authors say it needs replication. Stroke counted prevalent as well as incident cases.

anchors.extracted: All stroke OR 0.98 (0.90 to 1.07; 35 studies, 10 164 events in 145 063); non-drinkers 1.12 (0.98 to 1.28), drinkers 0.95 (0.83 to 1.07), P=0.139. Ischaemic stroke 0.83 (0.72 to 0.95), shown in appendix figure S13.
4339 ischaemic strokes, available only in a subsample; stroke covered all subtypes, incident and prevalent, fatal and non-fatal.

anchors.extracted: The authors call the small number of strokes and the pooling of subtypes an important limitation and say the ischaemic-stroke result in a subset needs replication.

key_findings.note: Hypertension (104 570 cases) is in the 1st paragraph, not Table 2; the locator names both.
The >=1000-event result is given in the text; its table (S10) is in the appendix.
Ischaemic stroke 0.83 is stated in the text; its forest plot is appendix figure S13.
The linkage-disequilibrium check used Whitehall II only (Methods › Statistical analysis, 6th paragraph).

key_findings.correction: The Methods state these expectations, but 'before the analysis' cannot be verified: no protocol or registration was published. Read: 'The Methods state that, if the U-shape were causal, ...'.

reporting_issues.note: For C-reactive protein the non-drinker interval includes 0 (-7.42 to 0.95), so only the point estimates match; for systolic pressure, interleukin-6 and BMI the intervals exclude 0.
The 'What this study adds' box uses the stronger 'is beneficial' wording, as the abstract does.

risk_of_bias.note: Overall some concerns for the pooled main result; I agree the stratified estimates carry a higher risk (conditioning on self-reported drinking). 'Prospective-cohort' is a labelling convention: the pooled 'epidemiological studies' are of mixed design (designs listed only in the appendix) and the outcomes include prevalent cases. The card's author-overlap notes are right: K Mukamal, E Rimm and G Davey Smith are on the Holmes author list.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: the abstract's 'beneficial even for light to moderate drinkers' rests on imprecise strata and a non-significant heterogeneity test, and the Discussion misdescribes the non-drinker biomarker results.
